stem: What is the primary anatomical definition of conjunctivitis as described in the lecture?

options.text: Inflammation of the mucous membrane lining the outer part of the eye and the inner eyelids.
Infection of the corneal epithelium that results in localized redness and blurred vision.
Inflammation of the lacrimal gland and the associated tear drainage system.
Swelling of the sclera caused by an autoimmune response to systemic allergens.

explanation: The conjunctiva is the mucous membrane that covers the sclera and lines the upper and lower fornices up to the edge of the cornea.
rationale: Consider which specific membrane lines the upper and lower fornices.

optionExplanations.A: The conjunctiva is the mucous membrane that covers the sclera and lines the upper and lower fornices up to the edge of the cornea.
optionExplanations.B: Infection of the cornea is referred to as keratitis, whereas conjunctivitis involves the surrounding mucous membrane.
optionExplanations.C: This describes dacryoadenitis or dacryocystitis, which are distinct from the inflammation of the conjunctival membrane.
optionExplanations.D: Inflammation of the sclera is scleritis, which is deeper and distinct from the superficial conjunctival inflammation.
